Cloud Console Hardening wave 4 - a boundary is a census, and a census must be pinned: land the live HEAD-burn, then machine-check every boundary the epic wrote in prose

Living wave Paper for the Cloud Console Hardening epic (bp task cloud-console-hardening-epic, 121 children: 110 open / 6 done / 4 in_progress / 1 cancelled). Charter: .claude/workflows/bp-cloud-console-hardening-charter.md - standing laws 1-7, decisions D1-D62, all of which now exist on origin/main (D60's fix, PR #5413). Predecessor Papers: cloud-console-hardening-wave-3-2026-07-21, cloud-console-hardening-wave-2-2026-07-21, cloud-console-hardening-wave-2026-07-21. Phases append below in order; someone opening this mid-wave sees exactly where the wave stands.

STATUS: SURVEYING - Strategize is complete and this Paper carries the direction, the direction debate and the survey plan. The 20-question survey fleet is next; Digest will append the digest + verify plan BEFORE the verifiers fly, Decide the decisions + wave plan BEFORE the builders fly, Review the debrief.

The wish

MODEL CONSTRAINT (hard): Fable 5 is spend-limited - every phase runs on Opus/Sonnet, and Decide MUST set builder_model:'opus' for EVERY slice, never 'fable'. THIS CYCLE: cloud-console-hardening WAVE 4 - MACHINE-CHECK THE BOUNDARIES. Wave 3 proved that a stated coverage boundary went FALSE inside the wave that wrote it. A comment is not a tripwire. Ratify D41, then pay it across the epic's other documented-but-unenforced boundaries. Root task: cloud-console-hardening-epic.

Two corrections to the brief, both verified by content before anything else

CORRECTION 1 - THE LIVE DEFECT IS STILL LIVE. The lead's notes say 'fix already merged in #5434'. It is not. gh pr view 5434 returns state=OPEN, mergeCommit=null, and the required check 'PR references an active task' is FAILURE. Verified by content on origin/main: git show origin/main:cloud/lib/barkpark_cloud/web/router.ex | grep side_effecting_get? returns exactly the three original clauses (providers=false at :527, oauth/:provider=true at :531, callback=true at :535) plus the catch-all false at :537. There is NO ["v1","events"] clause. Meanwhile the SSE ticket DID land - accounts.ex:2047 consume_sse_ticket/1, router.ex:1416 post "/v1/auth/sse-ticket", :1575 require_user_sse, and app.js carries events?ticket= (1 ref) with events?token= at 0. So on origin/main RIGHT NOW: plug(Plug.Head) rewrites HEAD to GET before matching, GET /v1/events consumes the single-use ticket, and any unfurler, monitor or link scanner that HEADs a stream URL destroys a live user's credential. Also absent from origin/main: router_head_fence_census_test.exs and router_sse_ticket_head_burn_test.exs - both live only on #5434's branch. This is the standing lesson firing on the report that carried it: a claim note is a worker's assertion; content on origin/main is the running system.

CORRECTION 2 - D41 DOES NOT NEED RATIFYING; IT NEEDS PAYING. D41 is already written into the charter on origin/main (landed via #5413, commit 0459001e9): 'A coverage boundary must be MACHINE-CHECKED. A comment is not a tripwire.' - and it explicitly COMPLETES D40 by citing bp-honest-gates D1 (cause + population + ratchet), D5 (ban the SHAPE, do not enumerate) and D11 (a committed baseline count CI forbids increasing is the sanctioned fallback where a full structural predicate is too expensive). Re-ratifying it would burn the wave reproducing a ruling that already exists. Wave 4's whole content is the payment.

Both corrections are the same discipline the lead asked for and are recorded here so no later phase re-inherits either. Wave 3 corrected the lead twice and was right both times; wave 4 does not re-inherit ERROR 1 (the mint fence is 'the PATH has no GET route', per D26 - source now says so at router.ex:1410) or ERROR 2 (D40 is narrowed to ENFORCEMENT MECHANISMS, never universal).

The direction - a boundary is a census, and a census must be pinned

Wave 4's thesis in one line: EVERY coverage boundary this epic has written is really a CENSUS STATED IN PROSE, and a census in prose cannot ratchet. That is not a metaphor - it is the measured shape of all five boundaries in the fence.

Measured on origin/main. Grepping the fence for boundary vocabulary (COVERAGE BOUNDARY / out of scope BY DECISION / do not grow this list / is a FLOOR, not a ceiling / does NOT cover / blind to) returns a small, tractable population: router.ex:501-508 (the HEAD deny-list - the one that went false), workers/sse_ticket_reaper.ex:46 (shipped in wave 3), __css_check.mjs:74-115 (shipped in wave 3, #5438), __preview__/smoke.mjs:484 (shipped in wave 3), app.css:3496 and __app.test.mjs:4719 (echoes of the same ruling). Wave 3 paid D40 well: every one of these STATES its boundary carefully. Not one of them is CHECKED.

And each makes exactly three kinds of claim, all three machine-checkable: (a) a COUNT - 'this list fences exactly TWO routes', 'the 45 authenticated GETs', 'five attribute-state writes, NOT the three earlier recon claimed', '8 unfixtured destructive DELETEs', '14 api(DELETE) call sites'; (b) a set of FILE:LINE CITATIONS - 52 of them across cloud/ (app.js:3312, :3344, :12013, :16442, :16445, :1021, :1112, :1050, :2295, :5430, :5474, :7381, :9991, adapter.ex:263, mutations.ex:273 and more); (c) a NAMED SIBLING CHECK that supposedly covers what this one does not - 'E5 owns them', 'already on main (#5377)', 'Full measurement lives on task cch-w2-head-sideeffect-fence'.

So the payment splits by CHECKABILITY, not by prose - and the split is what makes it D5-compliant rather than a hand list: CITATIONS get the ban-the-SHAPE treatment (universal, zero enumeration - path:NNN is a lexically exact token, so the gate's population is the text of the tree); COUNTS get the D11 declared-baseline treatment (opt-in pin, recomputed from source, CI forbids drift); NAMED SIBLINGS get an existence predicate (a boundary that delegates to a check somebody deleted is the same lie one level out).

Prior art is already shipped, working and CI-gated in this repo - the wave extends a proven mechanism rather than minting one. scripts/docs-anchors-check.sh section 3 already resolves 'Code anchors' lines to an existing path AND greps the declared symbol to a real definition; section 8 already parses in-code '@canonical capability:<slug>' markers, enforces slug uniqueness repo-wide, and requires a public def/func/export within 6 lines below. That is exactly the citation-plus-anchor predicate, pointed at docs. Wave 4 points the same mechanism at code comments inside the fence.

Two instruments, both IN FENCE, both riding gates that already exist - no new CI wiring and no dispensation beyond what wave 1 and wave 3 already granted: an ExUnit boundary test under cloud/test/ for the Elixir side (cloud.yml's test job runs a bare unfiltered mix test with a Postgres service, so a committed test file IS the gate the moment it lands), and a cloud/priv/static/__boundary_check.mjs for the JS/CSS side (console-harness.yml's path filters already glob cloud/priv/static/**). #5434's own router_head_fence_census_test.exs is the template to generalise, not merely an instance fix: it shipped the clause AND a census test AND a burn test - clause + machine check + a test that proves the check can fail.

This is also the composite proof, absorbed exactly as wave 3 absorbed Act 3 rather than deferred into new machinery. The moment both instruments land, any later slice that invalidates a boundary reds on MERGED main - which is precisely the failure mode that is invisible to every branch-local gate and visible in ten seconds side by side. Wave 2 ruled that a clean git merge is evidence of ancestry, never of behaviour; the HEAD-burns-ticket finding is that ruling's existence proof, and it is the THIRD instance of the co-scoped pattern in this epic and the FIRST one that was live.

EVERY machine check ships mutation-proven able to fail: remove the clause, watch it red, put it back, and record both directions. This repo has shipped vacuous greens before - a pathspec matching nothing returns exit 0; a harness mock that FAKED success reported '0 session(s) revoked' as a pass; D44 found a filed criterion whose population was literally EMPTY (0 of 62 GET routes reach a Repo write at depth 0 or 1). The wave's most reflexive payment is cch-w1-emit-fence-regression-test: the emit --write attribution fence can be deleted today and nothing reds. A check nobody has seen fail is a check nobody should trust.

ONE slice stays pointed at users, so the epic's vision does not collapse into developer navel-gazing. The vision is 'the console stops lying' - to operators, not only to builders. cch-bl-overview-background-refresh-fails-silently is a lie to a user AND a boundary at once: a persistently failing background fleet refresh paints stale instances with no signal, which is the exact shape D9 already ruled on one surface out (fixing a defect without a state to show it trades a security defect for an honesty defect). It is also where the Kinsta/Vercel bar is plainly unmet - those consoles say 'reconnecting' out loud.

What the finished experience feels like: open router.ex and the boundary comment is followed by a marker naming the test that holds it. Break any number in that prose and CI names the line and the true value. Delete the sibling check a boundary delegates to and CI says so. Add a side-effecting GET and the census pin reds with the route's name in it. And in the console itself, a fleet panel that has stopped refreshing SAYS it has stopped. The epic's instruments stop being able to decay quietly.

PRIORITIES, in order: (1) merge #5434 and get the live credential-burn off main - nothing else in this wave matters more than a defect that is live right now; (2) build the two boundary instruments and pay every in-fence boundary with them; (3) the ratchet fix on cssom-parity's one-way decaying floor (cch-bl-cssom-floor-decays-as-css-grows - D11's canonical shape, and the floor currently decays in the wrong direction); (4) the emit-fence reflexive gap; (5) the Overview honesty slice. Finished this wave: the boundary contract and the live defect. Started, not finished: the repo-wide promotion of the citation gate - that is wave 5's, and only if the measured stale rate says it can land clean.

The direction debate - four rivals, seriously developed

RIVAL A - 'N bespoke tests, one per boundary.' The literal reading of the wish, and the cheapest, lowest-risk shape: six small slices, each mutation-proven, each closing one filed row. WHY IT LOST: it re-creates hand-maintained enumerations, which is exactly the shape D5 bans ('a hand-maintained key list mis-matches both ways - ban the SHAPE, do not enumerate'), and it leaves NO ratchet, so the next boundary written in wave 5 is unpinned again. It buys instances and not the class - directly contradicting D41's own citation of bp-honest-gates D1 (a fix without a ratchet regrows). It is the first idea, and the wish asks for the class.

RIVAL B - 'the composite-merge CI job.' Attack the CAUSE rather than the symptom: the boundary went false because a SIBLING SLICE INSIDE THE SAME WAVE changed the world, so build a gate that tests the union of open PRs before any of them merges. Genuinely strong - it catches the joint defect BEFORE merge, where a post-merge machine check only reds main afterwards, and this repo is documented to let main sit red for hours ('Main Elixir gate silent jam'). WHY IT LOST, on three grounds: (i) it is new CI machinery outside a tight fence, in a wave that otherwise needs no dispensation at all; (ii) D58 measured that main carries NO branch protection and NO rulesets (404 'Branch not protected'), so a brand-new gate would be advisory-by-absence - the wave would ship an unenforced boundary while preaching against them; (iii) a landed machine check converts an invisible defect into a NAMED red on main, which is the honest outcome this epic actually wants. ABSORBED, NOT DROPPED: the reviewer runs every wave-4 check on the TRUE MERGED TREE of all wave-4 branches before merging and records the result - the ten-second side-by-side wave 2 ruled for and wave 3 proved out.

RIVAL C - 'the repo-wide citation-resolver gate as the headline.' Every file:NNN in every comment must resolve. This is the sharpest single instrument anywhere in the space: three citations went stale in ONE wave (cch-bl-source-citation-line-drift is filed on exactly that), and the repo is saturated with them. WHY IT LOST AS A HEADLINE: its blast radius is unmeasured and probably large. A gate that reds on two hundred pre-existing stale citations cannot land without a suppression baseline, and a suppression baseline is the hand list D5 bans - the rival defeats itself at scale. KEPT as predicate (b), scoped to the fence's measured 52 citations, where it can plausibly land with zero suppressions. The survey's first job is to measure the current stale rate; if it is small, wave 5 promotes it repo-wide with real evidence instead of hope.

RIVAL D - 'UX-led: go hit the Kinsta/Vercel bar.' The console's polish genuinely trails those products and there are filed rows for it. WHY IT LOST: the dark crown caps it. PLATFORM_ADMIN_EMAILS is unset on prod, lives in a gitignored .env, and zero deploy scripts reference it - NO COMMIT CAN SET IT - so every authenticated user gets 403 on the operator console and much of the surface cannot be seen by a human at all. A UX-led wave would spend its budget on claims it cannot prove. And the epic's frame is honesty, not polish. KEPT as exactly one slice, chosen because it is a lie to a user AND a boundary at once.

WHY THE WINNER WON: it is the only candidate that pays the CLASS with a mechanism whose population is the text of the tree rather than an enumerated set - which is the difference D5 draws between a fix that holds and a fix that regrows. It needs no new CI, no new dispensation, and it extends an instrument (docs-anchors-check.sh sections 3 and 8) that is already shipped, already gated and already proven in this repo. And it produces the composite proof as a by-product rather than as a second project.

THE SHARPEST ATTACK WE FOUND ON THE WINNER: 'The DISCOVERY half is the whole value, and it cannot be made reliable over natural-language prose. A regex over English will miss boundaries and invent them. Without reliable discovery, the boundary contract is a hand-maintained registry - D5's banned shape - and it will mis-match both ways, exactly like the key list D5 was written about.' This is correct and it very nearly killed the direction. HOW THE WAVE ABSORBS IT: do not discover boundaries by prose at all. Split the population by CHECKABILITY. Citations (path:NNN) are lexically exact, so they get UNIVERSAL coverage with no registry whatsoever - the gate walks every comment in the fence and there is nothing to maintain. Counts are genuinely fuzzy in English, so they get an OPT-IN declared pin, which is precisely D11's sanctioned fallback for the case where a full structural predicate is too expensive - and the pin carries its own mutation proof. The residue (a boundary that states no count and cites no line) is honestly unenforceable, and the wave SAYS SO in the boundary contract's own coverage boundary rather than pretending otherwise.

SECOND ATTACK: 'A boundary gate is itself an enforcement mechanism, so by D40 it must state its own coverage boundary, which by D41 must be machine-checked - infinite regress.' The regress terminates, and the reason is the direction's core claim: this gate's population is THE TEXT OF THE TREE, not an enumerated route set. A check whose population is 'every file:line citation in the fence' cannot go stale the way 'the two routes I listed' can, because nothing a future author writes escapes it. Its own boundary is stated, and its own mutation proof plants an unresolvable citation and watches it red.

THIRD ATTACK, the one the survey must settle before Decide: 'you assume the in-fence citations are mostly correct today.' If they are mostly stale, the gate cannot land clean and Rival A becomes the right answer after all. That is survey question citation-stale-rate, and it is load-bearing for the whole direction.
